ic_name: DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface, IEC 62386 via TI SLAA422A)
module_role: DALI control gear (LED driver / ballast subordinate) — receives 16-bit forward frames over the 2-wire DALI bus, validates address against this gear's Short Address / Group / Broadcast, executes the encoded direct-arc-power-level or indirect command, and answers query commands with an 8-bit backward frame. The gear maintains persistent variables (Power On Level, Min/Max Level, Fade Rate/Time, Short Address, Group, Scene 0..15, Random Address, Fast Fade Time, Failure Status, Operating Mode, Dimming Curve) in non-volatile storage, applies the logarithmic 254-level dimming curve to the LED driver, and exposes Configuration-Mode addressing commands (RANDOMIZE / COMPARE / WITHDRAW / SEARCH / PROGRAM / VERIFY / QUERY SHORT ADDRESS) for installation/commissioning.

integration_overview.host_side: Internal control-gear logic — Manchester encode/decode, address match, command dispatch, fade engine, persistent-variable store. No external CPU bus is mandated by IEC 62386.
integration_overview.wire_side_dali: DALI 2-wire bus, opto-isolated. DALI_RX edge-interrupt input + DALI_TX open-drain output. Voltage 9.5..22.5 V; current ≤ 250 mA.
integration_overview.wire_side_led_driver: LED driver enable + PWM compare outputs to TPS62260-class buck regulators. In SLAA422A: P1.0/P1.1 = TPS62260_ENABLE; P1.2/TA1 + P1.3/TA2 (F2131) or P1.6/TA0.1 + P1.4/TA0.2 (G2xx2) = PWM1/PWM2.
integration_overview.clock_source: Implementation-defined; SLAA422A uses MSP430 SMCLK = MCLK = 8 MHz from the integrated DCO.
integration_overview.reset_source: Power-on reset + brown-out detect; after reset Actual Level := Power On Level loaded from information memory.
integration_overview.interrupt_routing: DALI_RX edge → bit-level Manchester decode ISR; WDT+ interval → fade-tick ISR + special-command timeout; Timer_A3 CCR → PWM update on TI_DALI_Update_Callback.

interface_categories: DALI bus interface — DA+/DA- through opto-isolators to DALI_RX (interrupt-on-edge) and DALI_TX (open-drain).
LED driver interface — TPS62260_ENABLE GPIO + PWM1 + PWM2 to drive the buck regulators / LED strings.
Non-volatile storage interface — MSP430 information memory (FLASH) holding the 32-byte persistent variable layout of Table 2.
Debug interface — Spy-Bi-Wire / JTAG on the MSP430.
Optional external sensor / button input (DALI 2 control-device parts -301..-304).
interconnect_topologies_supported: Single-bus DALI universe — 1 control device + up to 64 short-addressed control gear + up to 16 group addresses + broadcast.
Multi-universe topology — multiple DALI buses bridged by a DALI router / gateway (e.g. DALI ↔ KNX, DALI ↔ Modbus, DALI ↔ Ethernet).

Mixed device-type bus — DT0 fluorescent + DT6 LED + DT8 colour + DT7 switching gear coexist on the same DALI bus; ENABLE DEVICE TYPE X (0xC1) selects the extended command set for the next forward frame.
DALI-2 input devices (IEC 62386-301..-304) coexist on the same bus as control gear; arbitration via the wired-AND bus + RANDOMIZE/COMPARE/WITHDRAW iteration.
default_signal_values_when_omitted: Persistent variables that have never been programmed take their factory-default values: Maximum Level = 254, Minimum Level = PHYS_MIN_LEVEL (90 in TI example), Fade Rate = code 7 (≈ 44 steps/s), Fade Time = code 0 (immediate), Short Address = 0xFF (unassigned), Group bitmaps = 0, Scene n = 0xFF (MASK), Power On Level = implementation-defined.
soc_dependent_items: Choice of microcontroller (MSP430F2131 in main body / MSP430G2xx2 value-line in Appendix B; any MCU with edge-interrupt GPIO + a millisecond-grade timer + a PWM peripheral can implement DALI).

Pin assignment for DALI_RX / DALI_TX, PWM1 / PWM2, TPS62260_ENABLE — abstracted via dali_demo_hw.h in the Appendix-B design (Table 6 lists the abstractions: TPS62260_ENABLE_PxOUT/BIT, PWM1_BIT, PWM2_BIT, DALI_RX_PxIN/PxIES/PxIFG/BIT, DALI_TX/BIT, GPIO_INIT(), TIMER_VECTOR, TAxCCR0/1/2, TAxCCTL1/2, TAxCTL, DUMMY_VECTORS).
PWM frequency / period — Table 1 of SLAA422A gives valid ranges for 1.6 kHz / 0.8 kHz / 0.4 kHz at 8 MHz SMCLK.
Watchdog Timer Plus interval vs Timer_A used for fade clock (the WDT+ smallest interval cannot reach the 25-ms fastest fade time without ≈ 10.16 MHz; § 3.2 of SLAA422A discusses the constraint).
Information-memory partitioning — the 32-byte variable area is split across multiple flash segments to multiply the 100 000-cycle endurance.
Opto-isolator selection — 4N137-class on the DALI side, with bus-side current-limit resistor + MCU-side pull-up.
LED string voltage / current — depends on TPS62260 feedback resistors R7/R9.
Power-fail detection — SLAA422A suggests Comparator_A+ to trigger TI_DALI_Flash_Update before VCC drops below 2.2 V; bus capacitance must hold VCC ≥ 2.2 V for ≥ 3 ms.

low_power_modes.n_a_at_protocol_layer: DALI does not standardize a sleep / wake protocol; gear must be ready to receive any forward frame at any time.
low_power_modes.implementation_strategies: Microcontroller may sit in LPM3/LPM4 between forward frames, woken by the DALI_RX edge interrupt; PWM and Timer_A3 may be gated when Actual Level = 0; TPS62260_ENABLE may be deasserted in OFF state.
low_power_modes.no_explicit_sleep_command: No DALI command places the gear into a low-power state; the System Failure Level + power-on behaviour are the only DALI-defined power-related behaviours.

compatibility_notes: TI SLAA422A predates the IEC 62386-101/102/103 split — it references IEC 60929 (the original) and lists IEC 62383-102 / IEC 62383-107 in the references (likely typo for 62386-102 / -107). Modern implementations should follow IEC 62386 directly.

Special command WRITE MEMORY LOCATION (0xC7) and indirect command ENABLE WRITE MEMORY (0x81 / cmd 129) are NOT supported in SLAA422A because the MSP430 flash erase/program time exceeds the 9.17 ms inter-frame settle.

Bank-1 memory map (used for IEC 62386-207 LED-specific extended parameters) is NOT supported in SLAA422A. Commands 224..227 (Reference System Power, Enable/Disable Current Protector, Select Dimming Curve), 242..251 (LED-specific queries) are also not supported; command 240 (QUERY EXTENDED VERSION NUMBER) must indicate this.
DALI is single-master per bus; coordinating multiple control devices requires application-layer token handoff or a single DALI router.

DALI-2 (post-2014) adds IEC 62386-103 control-device parts, certification by the DALI Alliance, and a stricter electrical conformance — backward-compatible with DALI-1 gear at the wire level but with stricter timing and Manchester tolerances.
